name: Amunet
loreTies: Source: Ma'at weighing of the heart + Ammit (punishment/devouring when the heart is heavy)
HUMAN_EGYPTIAN_LORE_AS_ECHO: courtroom scales are copies of Amunet's living prism verdict
The punishment side of truth: refraction that splits lies from being
shortBackstory: Amunet is the punishment side of Ma'at: when something refuses balance, he refracts its hidden weight until armor, lies, and false sanctity split open. Human scales of judgment are crude courtroom copies of his living prism verdict. He does not negotiate — he reveals.

chapters.title: Origin
chapters.text: Amunet was forged from the punishment half of Ma'at's scales — the side that devours what fails the weighing of the heart. He is not the feather of truth; he is what happens when the feather finds you wanting. His prism body refracts hidden weight into visible judgment light, splitting lies from truth like a prism splits white light into spectrum. Ancient humans glimpsed him through the Mythos Gate and carved courtroom scales as crude copies, but his living prism does not weigh evidence — it weighs being.

chapters.title: Faction Bond
chapters.text: Among the Aten Ra, Amunet is the one even other deities avoid. He is not cruel — he is precise. His function is to reveal what the faction cannot afford to hide from itself. When Aten-Ra's judgment grows too rigid, Amunet refracts the rigidity as tyranny. When Sutekh's chaos grows too useful, Amunet shows the cost. He does not serve the faction's comfort; he serves its truth, and truth in the Solar Dominion is not a virtue — it is a weapon that cuts the wielder first.

chapters.title: Gate Wound
chapters.text: The Mythos Gate wounded Amunet by showing him a truth he could not refract. The Hollow's erasure is not a lie — it is the absence of anything to judge. His prism, built to split hidden weight from visible form, found nothing to split. The scales balanced on emptiness. For the first time, Amunet's verdict was silence, and the silence was not judgment — it was helplessness. The wound taught him that a prism cannot refract what does not exist.

chapters.title: Campaign Role
chapters.text: In The First Reopening, Amunet is the breaker who shatters corrupted Gate defenses and reveals what the Hollow has hidden. His prism verdict splits open the Gate's lies, showing where the erasure has eaten the record. But against the Hollow, his power inverts — he must learn to fight absence rather than deception. The campaign tests whether truth, once forced into the open, can ever be undone — or whether his refraction destroys what it illuminates.

chapters.title: Personal Conflict
chapters.text: Amunet's flaw is that he cannot stop revealing. His prism nature means he shows everything — including the truths the Solar Dominion needs hidden to function. He has refracted Aten-Ra's certainty as tyranny, Sutekh's loyalty as violence, and Iset's mercy as weakness. His conflict: is truth always a service, or are there things that must stay hidden for civilization to survive? The punishment side of Ma'at was built to judge — but judgment without restraint is just destruction wearing a scale.
